name: Rio de Janeiro police war against Comando Vermelho
started: 2025-10-28 (Operation Containment, the deadliest police operation in Brazil's history)
summary: Rio de Janeiro's state police are waging large armed raids on favelas controlled by the Comando Vermelho, Brazil's oldest criminal faction. Operation Containment on 28 October 2025 left between about 121 and 132 dead, the highest toll of any police operation in Brazil's history, and big raids continued in 2026. Supporters see the raids as reclaiming territory; critics, including the UN rights office and President Lula, see massacres.

sides.name: Rio de Janeiro state security forces
members: Military Police, including the Special Operations Battalion (BOPE)
Civil Police, including its special operations unit (CORE)
leaders: Cláudio Castro (Governor of Rio de Janeiro state)
sides.strength: About 2,500 police committed to Operation Containment (Wikipedia, Operation Containment)

sides.name: Comando Vermelho (CV)
members: CV-controlled favela complexes in Rio's North Zone and centre
leaders: Edgard Alves de Andrade 'Doca' (main leader, escaped Oct 2025 operation)
sides.strength: Not estimated in the sources consulted

background: The Comando Vermelho controls dozens of favelas in Rio and has spread to other states, financed by drugs, extortion and control of local services. Rio's police have long relied on military-style incursions with armoured vehicles and helicopters, which produce high death tolls and periodic court-imposed limits. The debate matters nationally: the federal government favours a constitutional reform of public security, the US is weighing whether to designate the CV and the PCC as terrorist organizations, and Lula's government is lobbying against that designation.
year: On 28 October 2025 about 2,500 police with 32 armoured vehicles, BOPE demolition vehicles and two helicopters moved into the Alemão and Penha complexes and 26 surrounding communities. The CV answered with barricades, drones dropping bombs on special forces teams, and 71 hijacked buses used to block expressways. Residents recovered at least 70 bodies from woods near Penha the next morning. Police counted 117 suspects and 4 officers dead; the public defender counted 132. Police seized 93 rifles and about a tonne of drugs and arrested 133 people, but CV leader 'Doca' escaped and, per Reuters, none of the wanted men were killed.

The Supreme Court demanded explanations and the Senate opened an inquiry into organized crime. Raids continued: on 18 March 2026, about 150 BOPE officers in Santa Teresa killed at least eight people, including senior CV figure Claudio Augusto dos Santos and a resident taken hostage, and detained 116; a bus was burned in retaliation. In August 2026 another Military Police operation against the CV left four dead and 13 arrested.
situation: As of late October 2026 the CV retains its core territories, and Rio's police continue periodic large raids. The October 2025 operation remains under judicial and parliamentary scrutiny, and the question of US terrorist designations for Brazilian factions remains open.
technical: Operation Containment force: about 2,500 police, 32 armoured vehicles from the National Public Security Force, 12 BOPE demolition vehicles, 2 helicopters, plus all specialized Civil Police units (Wikipedia).
CV tactics: burning barricades, drones dropping explosives on BOPE and CORE teams, and 71 hijacked buses blocking Avenida Brasil and the Yellow and Red Lines.
Seizures: 93 rifles, some linked to the armies of Venezuela, Argentina, Peru and Brazil, and about one tonne of drugs.
Police losses: five officers killed (2 BOPE, 3 CORE) and 13 injured per Wikipedia's account; other counts give four police dead.
Of 115 dead identified by police, 108 had proven CV links and 59 had arrest warrants; Reuters found only five of 69 wanted men among those arrested and none among the dead.
Santa Teresa raid, 18 Mar 2026: about 150 BOPE officers with two armoured vehicles; 21 weapons, 105 kg of cocaine and 611 kg of marijuana seized (Última Hora).
Federal response: at least ten CV leaders moved to federal prisons after Oct 2025; a Senate inquiry into organized crime from Nov 2025.

Public opinion was split from official criticism: an AtlasIntel poll found 87.6 percent of Rio favela residents supported Operation Containment, while President Lula and the UN human rights office condemned it (Wikipedia; Última Hora).
Regional spillover: Argentina labelled the CV and PCC terrorist groups and raised its border alert, and Paraguay reinforced its border after the operation (Wikipedia).
casualties: Operation Containment, 28 Oct 2025: 117 suspects and 4 police dead per police (Wikipedia infobox), with other counts of 122 (police, later) and 132 (public defender, 128 civilians plus 4 police). Santa Teresa, 18 Mar 2026: at least 8 dead (Última Hora). Aug 2026 operation: 4 dead (Agência Brasil headline). No 12-month statewide total of deaths in police operations was found.

timeline.event: Operation Containment in the Alemão and Penha complexes leaves about 121 to 132 dead.
Senate inquiry into organized crime scheduled to begin.
BOPE raid in Santa Teresa kills at least 8, including a senior CV figure.

outlook: Watch for further mega-operations, court rulings on police lethality, and whether the US designates the CV and PCC as terrorist organizations, which would pull Brazil into Washington's regional 'narco-terrorism' framework.

sides: Rio de Janeiro state police (BOPE, CORE and others)
battles.outcome: Deadliest police operation in Brazil's history; 133 arrests and major weapons seizures, but CV leader 'Doca' escaped and none of the wanted men were killed (Reuters via Wikipedia).
battles.forces: About 2,500 police, 32 armoured vehicles, 12 BOPE demolition vehicles, 2 helicopters; CV used drones dropping explosives, burning barricades and 71 hijacked buses.
battles.losses: 117 suspects and 4 police killed per police (some accounts give 5 police); public defender counted 132 dead; 93 rifles and about 1 t of drugs seized (Wikipedia, Operation Containment).
battles.significance: Sparked a national debate over police lethality, a Supreme Court demand for answers and a Senate inquiry, and drew condemnation from the UN human rights office.
